title: Microfluidic system for in vitro epithelial folding and calcium waves induction
protocol: Put the polycarbonate disk in the plasma chamber with the crafted side facing up.
Close the chamber and turn on the vacuum pump to decrease the pressure inside the chamber to 0.1 mbar.
Prepare a parafilm slightly bigger than the polycarbonate disk on a bench.
Place a drop of 400 μL of freshly prepared APTES 1% v/v solution onto the parafilm.
Open the O2 bottle and the valves connected to the chamber when the pressure reaches 0.1 mbar in the chamber.
Turn on the O2 flow-meter to 2.0 nL/h and wait for the pressure inside the chamber to increase to ∼1 mbar.
Decrease O2 flow-meter to 0.2–0.3 nL/h to reach a pressure of 0.3–0.4 mbar in the chamber.
Activate plasma for a total of 60 seconds at the power of 10%.
Turn off the pump and fill the chamber with air to terminate the plasma cleaner cycle.
Using forceps, take the polycarbonate disk and place it on the 400 μL APTES drop with the activated side (side with engraved channel) facing down.
Incubate the polycarbonate for 20 minutes at 20°C–30°C.
Remove any air bubble trapped in the channel void by repositioning the system several times to ensure complete contact between the system and the APTES solution.
Prepare a container with 50–100 mL of ddH2O and a laboratory wash bottle with pure isopropanol, which will be used for washing the polycarbonate after the APTES treatment.
Cut a piece of 20 μm-thick PDMS membrane slightly bigger than the polycarbonate disk.
Place the PDMS film into the plasma chamber, with the PDMS layer facing up.
Remove the protection paper once the plastic film with the PDMS is positioned inside the chamber.
Secure the corners of the PDMS membrane with Magic scotch tape to prevent displacement during activation.
Activate the PDMS film using the plasma cleaner following steps 1 c–e.
Rinse the polycarbonate disk in a ddH2O water container using forceps.
Wash the APTES treated side of the polycarbonate disk thoroughly with isopropanol for 30 seconds.
Dry the polycarbonate disk with compressed air.
Place the polycarbonate disk with the channel facing down on the activated PDMS membrane.
Press firmly to start bonding from one side of the polycarbonate disk.
Remove some air bubbles locally with fingers if present.
Let the system react for 30 minutes at 20°C–30°C.
Inspect the fabricated system under a microscope for any problems such as entrapped dust or imperfectly bound membrane.
Discard systems presenting problems.
Remove the protection film from the PDMS gently from the edge of the system.
Use forceps and scalpel to remove the PDMS membrane above the inlet area.
Place the tubing connector facing up in the plasma chamber with the polycarbonate system.
Activate both PDMS surfaces (connector and system) by following steps 1c–e.
Align the connector and the inlet from the polycarbonate/PDMS system.
Put the two activated surfaces in contact for bonding.
Press gently to ensure full contact.
Wait at least 3 hours after plasma activation before proceeding to cell culture.
Insert the tubing into the fabricated connector on the system.
Connect the system with the pressure controller (pressure pump).
Submerge the system in a Petri dish filled with water.
Place the system submerged in the water-bath under an inverted microscope.
Observe if the PDMS membrane detaches from the polycarbonate upon increased pressure.
Verify by eye if no air bubbles are produced at the tubing connector or channel.
Sonicate the beads in the sonicator on high power to destroy bead clusters.
Dilute the nano-beads 1/200 in pure isopropanol.
Deposit a 20 μL drop of the diluted solution on a microscope slide.
Spread the solution with a pipette tip to create a larger area for deposition.
Dry the deposited solution at room temperature or accelerate drying at 40°C.
Place the microscope slide containing dried beads into direct contact with the microsystem channel region.
Repeat the bead deposition and drying steps multiple times to maximize bead coverage on the PDMS membrane.
Install the system upside down, with the channel facing the objective for inverted confocal microscopy.
Connect tubing and pressure controller to the system.
Use a confocal microscope with tile or multi-position option to create Z-stacks of the deformed membrane over the channel.
Typically use a 20× air objective (N.A. 0.5) on a Spinning Disk Andromeda RILL-FEI with EMCCD iXon 897 Camera.
Ensure standard Z-range limits are sufficient for imaging the deformed membrane.
Take a Z-stack over the non-deformed system.
Scan with different pressures to deform the membrane.
Calculate the curvature at the channel border from the obtained Z-stack.
Calculate the in-plane strain of the membrane using the relative position of nanobeads.
Wash out nanobeads from the PDMS system by scrubbing with soap and laboratory gloves.
Rinse the system thoroughly with water after washing.
Wait at least 3 hours for the PDMS membrane to recover from plasma treatment.
Place the system in a sterile container under the laminar hood.
Wash the system three times by fully submerging it in ethanol 70%.
Transfer the system into a new sterile container using forceps.
Wash the system three times with sterile PBS.
Coat the system with a sufficient amount of 40 μg/mL fibronectin solution in PBS to cover the PDMS surface but not the connector.
Leave the system one hour at 37°C.
Rinse the system carefully with PBS without introducing it inside the PDMS cube.
Remove the PBS.
Push the system toward the well bottom using sterile forceps or pipette tip to ensure fibronectin coating covers the entire system.
Add 2 mL of trypsin to the cells.
Incubate at 37°C until cells detach from the surface.
Centrifuge cells at 260 × g for 4 minutes.
Re-suspend the pellet in 2–3 mL of fresh culture medium.
Count MDCK cells and adjust concentration to deposit 3 × 10^5 cells per 1 cm² on fibronectin-coated system in S-MEM with 5% FBS, 1% antibiotic, and 5 μM CaCl₂.
Wash the system once with normal MEM complete medium after two hours.
Incubate the system in a cell incubator (5% CO₂; at 37°C) for 24 h.
Incubate cells with a calcium fluorescent probe (Fluo-4 Direct Calcium).
Filter dead or non-attached cells from the culture medium.
Aspirate 500 μL of medium into a syringe.
Fix a 0.20 μm filter and gently return 500 μL of medium to the well with the system.
Install the system in the microscopy holder using forceps.
Ensure correct installation and no medium leakage from the bottom.
Add double concentrated Fluo-4 Direct Calcium probe solution to an equal volume of medium.
Mix gently.
Incubate the system for 1 hour in the cell incubator.
Install the system on the inverted microscope stage.
Connect the system via tubing to the pressure controller.
Use a 20× objective for visualization.
Adjust the focus.
Use minimal excitation source power that ensures good quality fluorescence signal.
Position the field of view so that the border of the channel is visible on the image.
Adjust time-lapse observation settings to capture an image every two seconds for one minute.
Verify if observation settings are not phototoxic by taking a control time-lapse observation very far from the channel.
Start a time-lapse and acquire the first 5 frames before turning on the pressure (ΔP = -450 mbar).
Turn on the pressure controller once the initial frames are acquired.
Observe cellular deformation followed by an increase in calcium signal fluorescence.
Turn off the pressure controller to return to atmospheric level.
Detach the tubing after turning off the pressure controller.
Fix cells using standard procedures and proceed with immunofluorescence staining.
Mount samples with mounting medium and a coverslip for observation.
Cut off the connector using a scalpel.
Wash the system gently under water and with soap to remove cell culture reagents.
Secure the inlet of the system with tubing closed at one end with a needle and luer lock.
Insert the system into a small plastic bag and fill it with RIPA buffer.
Place the bag in a sonicator bath and ensure it is fully submerged in the lysis buffer.
Run two cycles of 4 min at the highest power using the sonicator bath.
Install and open ImageJ.
Upload the acquired video into ImageJ.
Adjust the scale and time resolution of your experiment.
Go to Image>Image Properties.
Set the scale of the image by filling pixel width and pixel height (set units to μm).
Set the frame interval to 2 seconds.
Select “global” if analyzing multiple images with the same properties.
Rotate the image so that the channel is positioned parallel to the left border of the image.
Go to Image>Transform>Rotate…
Set the angle of rotation and check with Preview if the transformation was correct.
Validate with OK.
Subtract the Fluo-4 Direct base signal to analyze only changes in fluorescence triggered by epithelial deformation.
Duplicate last image in sequence before pressure was turned on.
Go to Image>Duplicate.
Choose to not duplicate the whole stack by unclicking stack.
Go to Process>Image calculator and choose your time-lapse image as Image 1 and Duplicated image as Image 2.
Choose Subtract in the Operation panel.
Validate with OK.
Analyze distance calcium wave have spread.
Select the time-point of interest.
